subjects.note: invented man about 45, near three-quarter seen from his side and a little above, lying on his back with the head tilted up; near eye clenched shut (crow's feet, bunched cheek), far eye open and aiming; closed-mouth grin pulled up at one corner; stubble; slightly out of the focal plane (soft, photographic depth of field)

one hand held up at arm's length: loose fist, thumb extended with the nail toward his eye, as a sight to cover the moon; knuckle creases, nail edge and tendons are the focal plane (sharpest edges in the drawing)
lying supine on grass, arm straight up and taut along his line of sight, neck flexed a little to look along it; only head, shoulder and arm in frame
adult man in his mid-forties: stubble, a crisp brow and jaw, first lines at the eye corners, a few grey hairs at the temple; must not read as a boy or as a specific real person
short dark hair pressed into the grass, out of focus
the sleeve of a pale cotton shirt slipping down the raised forearm, a few folds at the elbow
grass blades very close to the lens at the frame's lower edge and around the head, blurred out of focus (bokeh), a few sharp ones at the head
clear afternoon sky as a filtered black-and-white photograph renders it: darker grey at the zenith to lighter toward the horizon, a few thin cirrus streaks so it is not an empty block

the daytime waxing gibbous moon, small (true angular size 0.5 degrees through the lens), the brightest and hardest-edged small shape; lit limb toward the sun's side, faint maria; it sits on the extension of the eye-thumb sightline (its vanishing point), visible to us though hidden to him
one late-afternoon sun, low, from the side; soft penumbras on the face, the eye socket and nose shadow, the hand's cast shadow, skylight filling the shadows
lens perspective of a close wide-angle shot: the head very near, the hand at arm's length, the moon at infinity; shallow depth of field with the focal plane on the hand
